irac.issue: Whether the substituted Section 15 of the Land Acquisition Act affects the right of the parties which accrued to them on the date of suit or on the date of passing of the decree by the Court of the first instance, and whether the decision in K. Chinnathambi Gounder was rendered per incuriam.
irac.rule: The substituted Section 15 does not affect the right of the parties which accrued to them on the date of suit or on the date of passing of the decree by the Court of the first instance as it has been introduced prospectively. The maxim 'actus curiae neminem gravabit' does not apply in this case. A decision rendered per incuriam is not binding if it is given in ignorance of the terms of a statute or of a rule having the force of a statute.
irac.application: The present appeals are unaffected by change in law in so far it related to determination of the substantive rights of the parties and the same are required to be decided in light of law of preemption as it existed on the date of passing of the decree. The decision in K. Chinnathambi Gounder was rendered prior to the amendment by 1984 Act and is not per incuriam.
irac.conclusion: The view expressed in Narasimhaiah's case and Nanjudaiah's case is not correct and is over-ruled. The decision in Pune Municipal Corporation is not a binding precedent as it was rendered on a question which was not germane to the case.
